items.title:
Anthropic has filed for an IPO, with its prospectus revealing just how fast the company is scaling.
FY25 revenue jumped 1,088% YoY to $4.59B, while compute and infrastructure spending rose 190% to $7.33B.
The company posted an $8.06B operating loss and ended 2025 with $20.28B in cash and short-term investments.
Anthropic’s two largest direct customers accounted for 24% of total revenue combined.
items.title_ja:
Anthropic は IPO を申請しており、その目論見書により同社がいかに急速に拡大しているかが明らかになりました。
25 年度の収益は前年比 1,088% 増の 45 億 9000 万ドルとなり、コンピューティングとインフラストラクチャへの支出は 190% 増の 73 億 3000 万ドルとなりました。
同社は80億6000万ドルの営業損失を計上し、2025年終了時点では202億8000万ドルの現金と短期投資を残した。
Anthropic の 2 つの最大の直接顧客は、合計収益の 24% を占めました。

Anthropic has committed about $900.9 billion to compute and infrastructure, and $70.7 billion of it comes due in the 12 months after September 30, per its final prospectus.
About $451.6 billion is expected to be spent before the end of 2030.
Its own chart shows revenue per dollar of compute at 1.72x in the third quarter, $17.0 billion of revenue against $9.9 billion of compute and infrastructure expense, up from 0.40x in the first quarter of 2025.
items.title_ja:
最終目論見書によれば、Anthropic はコンピューティングとインフラストラクチャに約 9,009 億ドルを投入しており、そのうち 707 億ドルが 9 月 30 日以降の 12 か月以内に支払期限を迎えます。
2030年末までに約4,516億ドルが支出されると予想されている。
同社のグラフによると、第 3 四半期のコンピューティング 1 ドルあたりの収益は 1.72 倍となり、コンピューティングおよびインフラストラクチャ費用 99 億ドルに対して収益 170 億ドルとなり、2025 年第 1 四半期の 0.40 倍から増加しています。

items.title:
Anthropic's final prospectus sets its lock-ups: up to 365 days for its co-founders and holders of more than 0.5% of fully diluted shares, and up to 180 days for others.
But 3.7 billion shares in the 180-day lock-up may become eligible for sale before it ends. That includes up to 10% of the locked-up shares held by non-founder directors, officers and employees, which can be sold from the first trading day.
Board members and affiliated entities have also indicated interest in buying up to $305 million of IPO shares, though the indications are not binding.
items.title_ja:
Anthropic の最終目論見書ではロックアップが設定されており、共同創設者および完全希薄化後の株式の 0.5% 以上の保有者については最大 365 日、その他の場合は最大 180 日となっています。
しかし、180日間のロックアップ期間中の37億株は、終了前に売却対象となる可能性がある。これには、創設者以外の取締役、役員、従業員が保有するロックアップ株式の最大10％が含まれており、取引初日から売却できる。
取締役会メンバーおよび関連団体も、最大3億500万ドルのIPO株の購入に関心を示しているが、この兆候には拘束力はない。

items.title:
Happy Anthropic IPO day. Shares of the Claude maker start trading on Nasdaq today under $ANT, around midday.
It priced at $83, above its $70-$78 range, selling 980 million shares for $81.34 billion. Reuters calls it the biggest IPO ever, and it values the company at about $1.5 trillion.
Overnight, shares were indicated more than 20% higher in grey-market trading, per Bloomberg.

items.title:
Chinese AI and lab-robotics company MegaRobo has raised nearly $200 million from investors including Oman's sovereign wealth fund, the Oman Investment Authority, per Bloomberg.
CMB International also joined, along with existing backers Asia Investment Capital, Granite Asia and Sinovation Ventures. MegaRobo did not disclose its valuation.
Its last big raise was a $300 million Series C in 2022, led by GGV Capital, Asia Investment Capital and Goldman Sachs.

CMB International も、既存の支援者である Asia Investment Capital、Granite Asia、Sinovation Ventures とともに参加しました。メガロボは評価額を明らかにしていない。
最後の大規模調達は、GGVキャピタル、アジア・インベストメント・キャピタル、ゴールドマン・サックス主導による2022年のシリーズCで3億ドルだった。

items.title:
Anthropic raised about $81 billion in its upsized IPO, selling roughly 980 million shares at $83, up from the 825 million it first planned, per Reuters.
Reuters calls it the biggest IPO ever. It tops the $75 billion SpaceX raised in June, though SpaceX reached $85.7 billion after its underwriters bought extra shares.
Anthropic itself sold about 956 million of the shares; existing holders sold the rest.
items.title_ja:

ロイターはこれを史上最大のIPOと呼んでいる。これはスペースXが6月に調達した750億ドルを上回っているが、引受会社が追加株を買い取ったことでスペースXは857億ドルに達した。
アンスロピック自体は約9億5,600万株を売却した。既存のホルダーが残りを売却しました。

It scaled up the deal late Wednesday after a glut of demand. With a $26 billion private placement from Nvidia, Microsoft and Google, it will have over $200 billion on its balance sheet.

Anthropic is weighing pricing its IPO at up to $85 a share, above its $70-$78 range, per Bloomberg.
At $85, the 825 million shares on offer would raise about $70 billion, or $81 billion with the extra allotment. That would still fall short of SpaceX's record $85.7 billion.

items.title:
Bret Taylor's AI agent startup Sierra is in talks to raise money at a $30 billion valuation, per The Information.
That's nearly double the $15.8 billion it was valued at in May, and triple its $10 billion valuation in September 2025.
items.title_ja:
The Information によると、ブレット・テイラー氏の AI エージェントのスタートアップである Sierra は、評価額 300 億ドルで資金調達に向けて交渉中だという。
これは5月時点の評価額158億ドルのほぼ2倍で、2025年9月時点の評価額100億ドルの3倍となっている。

items.title:
Lyme disease vaccine developer VitriVax raised $87 million in a Series C from investors including F-Prime, NEA, Eli Lilly and Sanofi Ventures.
There's no approved Lyme vaccine for people today. The only one that ever reached the market, LYMErix, was pulled in 2002.

現在、人々に使用できる承認されたライムワクチンはありません。これまでに市場に出回った唯一の LYMErix は 2002 年に廃止されました。

大企業向け統合人事システム「COMPANY」を手がけるWHIホールディングスが、東証プライム市場への上場承認を受けました。上場日は12月15日です。
想定仮条件は2,340〜2,590円で、平均の2,465円で計算すると時価総額は約3,813億円。
2026年のIPOでは時価総額、調達規模ともに最大の案件です。
新株の発行はなく、既存株主による売り出しのみです。売出株数はオーバーアロットメントを含めると約4,915万株、約1,211億円になります。
グローバル・オファリングで、主幹事は野村證券、SMBC日興証券、BofA証券、ゴールドマン・サックス証券です。
前身のワークスアプリケーションズが次世代製品「HUE」の開発失敗と顧客との訴訟で経営難に陥り、2019年8月に会社分割で切り出したHR事業をベインキャピタルが取得しました。取得額は約1,000億円とみられています。
2023年7月、ベインは新ファンドから再出資し、シンガポール政府系ファンドのGICとの共同保有に移行しました。
その後、2024年にサイダスを約66億円、2025年にエンバーポイントを約228億円で取得しました。エンバーポイントはベイン傘下からの取得です。現在の保有比率は、完全希薄化ベースでベイン56.78%、GIC39.88%です。
2025年12月期は、売上収益657億円（前期比21.9%増）、調整後EBITDAは305億円（同27.2%増）で、マージンは46%でした。2026年1〜9月期は、売上収益562億円（同18.0%増）、調整後EBITDA291億円（同23.0%増）で、マージンは52%まで上がっています。
一方、最終損益は1〜9月期で赤字です。借り換えに伴う手数料の一括費用化や、合併で税務上の繰越欠損金を一部引き継げなかったことが響きました。
顧客基盤の強さは際立っています。
・導入先：約1,200法人グループ
・年間解約率：1.0%
・NRR：112%
・契約10年以上の顧客：66%
・クラウド比率：2021年末の16.8%から2026年9月末に81.5%
大企業の給与計算は一度入れると替えにくく、クラウド移行による単価アップを着実に取り込んでいます。
2023年の再出資時の株主資本は約1,547億円、1株1,000円です。想定価格2,465円なら株式ベースで約2.5倍、約3.4年のIRRで30%前後と試算できます。
純有利子負債は約1,750億円で、時価総額に足した企業価値は約5,560億円で、直近12カ月の調整後EBITDA約359億円に対するEV/EBITDAは約15.5倍です。10月に報じられた「企業価値ベースで5,000億円超」になっています
ただし、今回売却するのは保有株の3割程度にとどまり、上場後もファンドが約3分の2を保有し続ける計算です。
リターンの大半は上場後の株価次第で、残りを段階的に売っていく形になります。
2019年取得分のベイン旧ファンドは、企業価値ベースで約1,000億円から約3,500億円へ約3.5倍にしていて、レバレッジを考えると、株式ベースのリターンはそれ以上です。

『道徳の真諦に至る』（2026年11月16日 16:25）
「君子の学におけるや、焉（これ）を蔵し、焉を脩し、焉に息し、焉に游（あそ）ぶ」（『礼記』）――私が私淑する明治の知の巨人・安岡正篤先生は「道徳の真諦（しんてい）」につき此の「学」同様に、「無理に押しつけて型に嵌（は）めることでは決してない。いろいろのものにぶつかり、争い、苦しんで、まごまごするのではなくて、いつもゆったりと、自然に進んで往く」と、御著書『先哲が説く指導者の条件』の中で述べておられます。
国語辞書を見ますと、真諦とは「事物や思想の根本にあるもの。本質をとらえた極致」と書かれています。常に大事な境地として追求されるべきは、こせこせせず、まごまごするのではなく、躁（さわ）がないということでしょう。本ブログでは以下、道徳の真諦に至る一法につき簡潔に私の考え方を申し上げておきます。
それは一言で言えば、中国清朝末期の偉大な軍人・政治家で太平天国の乱を鎮圧した曾国藩が唱える、「四耐四不（したいしふ）」の実践です。即ち「艱難汝を玉にす」と己に言い聞かせ、「冷に耐え、苦に耐え、煩に耐え、閑に耐え、激せず、躁がず、競わず、随（したが）わず」以て大事を成すのであります。ちなみに、曾国藩というのは安岡先生なども非常に尊敬されておられました。
例えば煩に耐えるということでは以前、当ブログ「北尾吉孝日記」（25年10月24日）で次のエピソードを御紹介したことがあります――斉（せい）の国の役人が、孟子に言われて王を諫（いさ）めたが容いれられず、辞職した。ある人が孟子に「あなたはどうする」と迫った。すると孟子は「我に官守（官職）無し、我に言責（げんせき）無し、則ち吾の進退、豈（あに）綽綽（しゃくしゃく）然として余裕有らずや」（私には官職もなく、諫める責任もない。だから私の進退は、ゆったりと余裕があるのだよ）と言った。自分は斉の国に王道（王者のとる正しい道）を説きに来たのだから、こせこせしない、というのである。多事に忙殺されるのではなく、煩に耐えるということは余裕綽綽という境地に達するということです。
あるいは閑に耐えるということは、意外と難しいと思います。高い精神性なかりせば、閑に耐えることが四耐の中では最も難しいのかもしれません。A級戦犯として絞首刑に処せられた広田弘毅内閣総理大臣（第32代）は「風車 風が吹くまで 昼寝かな」という句を詠んでいますが、このような句を詠めるとは大変な人物だと思います。人間、社会や人から求められない時期は、寂しさに耐えなければなりません。
仏教でも忍辱（にんにく：耐え忍ぶこと）として忍ということを悟る為の一つの修行としていますが、上記「四耐四不」全てを実践して行く中で次第に人物が大きくなって行き、道徳の真諦に近付いて行くのではないでしょうか。明治から昭和の国語教育者・芦田惠之助先生も「自分を育てるものは結局自分である」と言われるように、我々は不断の努力を重ね自らを磨き上げて人物と成るのです。
最後に本ブログの締めとして、出光興産創業者・出光佐三さんの言葉を御紹介しておきます。出光さんのような境地に達すべくは、修養というものを深く知り、好きになるまで耐え続けねばならないのだろうと思います――僕は人間というものは苦しいものと思っている。苦しみは死ななければなくならない。しかし、その苦労は無意味なものではない。苦労をすればするほど人間らしくなる。僧侶とか学者とか、現実的でない人は死ぬまで修養している。修養は今の人に言わせれば苦しみである。僕に言わせれば、その苦しみを楽しみとするのだ。しかし、僕もはじめは修養を非常に苦しみと思った。どうしてこんなに苦しむのかと思ったが、それを苦しみと思っていたのではしょうがないから、しまいに、それを楽しみに思うように変えただけの話である。

PEファンドは、銀行から借入しても、金利負担ゼロ。
その仕組みが、年12〜15%のリターンを生み出している。
❶ VCファンドとPEファンドの利回りの差は3倍以上
VCとPEの構造は根本的に違う。
・VCファンド：薄く広くたくさんの会社にばら撒く
・PEファンド：狭く深く1つの会社に入り込む
そしてリターンは、
・日本のVCファンドの平均：年0〜5%
・PEファンドの平均：年12〜15%
つまりPEファンドの方が、圧倒的に高い利回りを出せる構造になっている。
⇒ 薄く広くより狭く深くの方が、結果利回りが高い。
❷ PEの高利回りの秘密は銀行レバレッジ
なぜPEはこれほど高いリターンが出せるのか?
「レバレッジを使うから」
・エクイティ（自己資金）だけでなく銀行から借入する
・その借入で投資規模を膨らませる
・膨らませた分リターンも大きくなる
これで、自己資金以上の投資が可能になり、利回りが跳ね上がる。
⇒ PEの高リターンは銀行レバレッジの使い方で決まる。
❸ しかも金利負担は買収先の会社が担う仕組み
さらに、PEの構造で極めて優秀な部分がここ。
・銀行から借入するのはファンド
・でも、その金利負担は買収先の会社が担う
・つまりファンド自身は金利負担ゼロ
これで、こういう構造になる。
・レバレッジで投資規模を大きくできる
・でも、金利コストはファンドの利益を圧迫しない
・買収先の会社が生み出すキャッシュフローで、金利を返済する
・結果、ファンドの利回りが跳ね上がる
つまりレバレッジ × 金利負担なしの掛け算でPEは高リターンを構造的に生み出せる。
⇒ PEの本質はレバレッジで拡大、金利は買収先が負担の構造にある。
年商 数億円規模に伸ばすために、
・薄く広くより狭く深くのスタンスを選択する
・レバレッジの仕組みを正しく理解する
・優れたビジネスモデルの構造を自社の設計に応用する
どちらを選ぶかで、事業の戦い方は大きく変わる。

Anthropic has officially priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its original expected range of $70–$78, with trading expected to begin on the Nasdaq tomorrow.
This is one of the largest IPOs in stock market history and a major moment for the AI industry. The company increased its offering from 825 million shares to 980 million shares, bringing the total offering to approximately $81.3 billion. Of that, Anthropic itself will receive roughly $79.4 billion before fees, while existing shareholders will receive approximately $2 billion. This gives Anthropic an enormous amount of additional capital to invest in computing infrastructure, model training, and expanding its operations. What's particularly interesting is the valuation. At $83 per share, Anthropic is reportedly valued at approximately $1.08 trillion on a basic share count basis and around $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. Revenue growth has been extraordinary, reaching $33.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, compared with $4.6 billion for all of 2025. However, the company is still operating at a loss and faces enormous computing costs.
I think the timing is especially interesting considering all the concerns surrounding AI spending, valuations, and the sustainability of the AI trade. Yet Anthropic has managed to price above its original range while increasing the number of shares offered, suggesting institutional demand remains incredibly strong. That said, a successful IPO doesn't necessarily make it a great investment at any price. Competition from OpenAI, Google, and other frontier labs remains intense, and investors are already pricing in years of extraordinary growth. I'll be watching where the stock actually opens tomorrow because retail investors aren't guaranteed the $83 IPO price, and a significant opening premium could make an already expensive valuation even harder to justify.

Hedge funds are selling tech stocks like the AI trade is officially over.
According to Goldman Sachs, hedge funds are selling technology stocks at a pace we haven't seen in nearly a decade. Their long to short ratio in tech has also fallen to its lowest level since 2016, which tells you just how aggressively institutions are reducing their exposure. And I think a lot of this has to do with how crowded the AI trade became over the past couple of years. Many of these funds made enormous amounts of money investing in AI companies, but now they're worried about protecting those gains as concerns around valuations, AI spending, and the sustainability of the entire AI infrastructure buildout continue growing. And to be fair, I can understand some of those concerns. We're talking about hundreds of billions of dollars being invested into AI infrastructure, and investors are increasingly questioning when these companies will start seeing meaningful returns on that spending.
But here's what I find interesting. A lot of these companies are still reporting incredible revenue growth, demand for AI infrastructure remains strong, and their underlying businesses haven't necessarily deteriorated nearly as much as their stock prices would suggest. I think we're seeing a combination of legitimate concerns and hedge funds simply wanting to get out of the way before things potentially get worse. And here's the other side of this. When institutions have already sold this aggressively, you have to wonder how much selling pressure is actually left. If earnings continue holding up and sentiment improves, these same funds could eventually have to come back and buy the stocks they just sold. Now, I'm not saying we've reached the bottom, because things could absolutely get worse from here. Jensen Huang might actually be making a comeback to NVIDIA and things are getting pretty interesting behind the scenes.
According to a new exclusive report from Semafor, some NVIDIA board members are continuing to push for Jensen Huang to return as CEO, despite the company publicly stating that it has no plans to bring him back. Apparently, there's a faction within the board that believes reinstating Jensen would be the right decision, which suggests the board might not be as united as NVIDIA wants investors to believe. Jensen himself has already said he would be honored to return if the board decided it was in NVIDIA's best interests. So the biggest obstacle right now isn't necessarily Jensen's willingness to come back, but rather whether the directors opposing his return can be convinced to change their minds.
Meanwhile, NVIDIA is reportedly considering other candidates, including Arm CEO Rene Haas and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy. However, Haas reportedly has concerns about taking the job while there's still a public campaign to bring Jensen back. And honestly, I can't blame him. Imagine becoming CEO of NVIDIA while half the industry is calling for your predecessor to return. Another interesting detail is that Jensen still owns roughly 3.5% of NVIDIA, which could potentially give him some influence over the board through shareholder voting mechanisms. That doesn't guarantee anything, but it means he's not entirely powerless in this situation.
Personally, I think bringing Jensen back would be a massive positive for NVIDIA, especially given everything that's happened over the past week. The company just delivered incredible earnings, but there are still questions surrounding its leadership, the ongoing investigations, and whether it can maintain the same execution without the person who helped build it into what it is today. I'm not saying Jensen is definitely coming back, especially with the investigations still hanging over everything, but I think the possibility is becoming harder to dismiss. And if more directors start supporting his return, things could change pretty quickly.
Melvin (@MelvinInvests)
If you own ANY AI stocks, you need to read this.
“Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us. And employees are committed.” That was how NVIDIA's interim CEO Colette Kress ended what might be one of the most important earnings calls in the company's history. NVIDIA came into this quarter facing some serious concerns. Jensen Huang's departure, circular financing, the sustainability of AI spending, declining margins, export restrictions, and whether the company could continue executing without its founder. And I think management did a pretty good job addressing most of them.
First, the numbers were absolutely incredible. NVIDIA reported $116 billion in quarterly revenue, more than doubling year over year and growing 20% sequentially. Data center revenue reached $108 billion, up 21% quarter over quarter, while Vera Rubin generated nearly $20 billion in its first quarter of production shipments, making it the fastest product ramp in NVIDIA's history. Management also guided for $130 billion in Q4 revenue and raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook from 70% to 75%. Think about that for a second. We're talking about a company already generating more than $100 billion in quarterly revenue that still expects 75% annual growth in fiscal 2028. One of the biggest concerns was obviously Jensen Huang's departure. Interestingly, Jensen was only mentioned twice by name during the entire call. It almost felt like management wanted to distance the conversation from Jensen and shift investors' attention back to the business. The board explicitly stated that Jensen would not return as CEO and refused to discuss the ongoing investigation. Instead, Colette emphasized that NVIDIA's employees, leadership team, customers, and suppliers remain fully committed. She even mentioned that TSMC's leadership had been in NVIDIA's offices this week. The company also confirmed that Vera Rubin Ultra remains on track for next year, with Feynman expected in 2028. Now, despite the board saying Jensen isn't coming back, I personally still think there's a small chance we could eventually see him return in some capacity. I wouldn't bet on it, but I wouldn't completely rule it out either.
Another major concern was circular financing, particularly NVIDIA's financial relationships with neoclouds and other AI infrastructure companies. Investors have been worried that NVIDIA is essentially financing customers who then purchase its GPUs. Management clarified that many of its guarantees only take effect once customers have secured financing and their infrastructure is ready for deployment. If those conditions aren't met, certain commitments can be reduced or eliminated. Colette also confirmed this wasn't a new policy, just additional disclosure explaining how the arrangements work. That doesn't eliminate the risk, especially with NVIDIA carrying $118 billion in guarantees and $32 billion in neocloud related commitments, but it does provide more transparency. And speaking of neoclouds, I thought this was one of the most bullish parts of the entire call for companies like $NBIS and $CRWV. NVIDIA's AI Cloud, Industrial, and Enterprise segment generated $47 billion in revenue, growing 18% sequentially and nearly tripling year over year. Management emphasized that neoclouds are becoming increasingly important to the AI ecosystem, helping enterprises, governments, and AI labs access computing capacity.
NVIDIA revealed that Hopper GPUs are being recontracted at up to twice their original rental prices, while B300 rental rates have increased more than 60% since introduction. Management also confirmed that its compute remains fully utilized across every hyperscaler and neocloud it serves. That's a pretty big deal because one of the biggest bearish arguments against neoclouds has been that their expensive GPUs would rapidly lose value as newer hardware became available. Instead, we're seeing older GPUs retain significant economic value while newer hardware commands higher rental rates. $NBIS jumped more than 12% following those comments, and I think it's pretty clear why. If these pricing and utilization trends continue, the economics for well positioned neocloud operators could be considerably better than many investors expected. Another concern was whether the AI infrastructure boom was approaching its peak. NVIDIA pushed back with some pretty incredible numbers. Cloud industry backlog increased from $2 trillion to $2.5 trillion in just three months, while hyperscaler cloud revenue growth accelerated for the sixth consecutive quarter. Meanwhile, token volumes on OpenRouter increased 35 times year over year, with AI agents now accounting for approximately 80% of tokens. Token prices have also declined nearly 60% since May, encouraging significantly greater usage. Essentially, AI is becoming cheaper to use, but consumption is growing so quickly that demand for computing infrastructure continues to accelerate.
Margins were another major topic. NVIDIA expects Q4 gross margins to decline to 71%–72%, but management explicitly described that quarter as the bottom, with margins expected to recover to 72%–73% in fiscal 2028. Colette explained that NVIDIA had honored existing purchase orders despite rising supply costs and expects updated pricing to help stabilize margins. That's reassuring considering the concerns around memory costs, advanced packaging, and competition from custom AI chips. Management also addressed supply constraints, confirming that NVIDIA has secured additional memory and advanced packaging capacity. Vera Rubin is being deployed roughly twice as fast as Grace Blackwell, with hyperscalers bringing the platform into production in approximately one month. NVIDIA is also prioritizing customers that have secured financing, sufficient power, and data centers ready to deploy its hardware. That's particularly important because demand means very little if customers can't actually install and operate the infrastructure.
There were also questions about a potential slowdown in 2028 due to political uncertainty, electricity constraints, and opposition to data center construction. Management acknowledged those risks but emphasized that customers are still requesting more supply than NVIDIA can currently deliver. The company also established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to strengthen engagement with the US government. Importantly, its guidance already excludes future licensed Hopper shipments to China, although the latest export restrictions are still being evaluated. Another encouraging development was capital allocation. NVIDIA returned $28 billion to shareholders during the quarter, including $22 billion in buybacks and $6 billion in dividends. It also increased its repurchase authorization by $150 billion, leaving $227 billion available at quarter-end. Management intends to execute that authorization by the end of fiscal 2028 while continuing to invest in supply chain expansion and selected infrastructure partnerships.

If you own ANY AI stocks, you need to read this.
“Our momentum is real. Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us. And employees are committed.” That was how NVIDIA's interim CEO Colette Kress ended what might be one of the most important earnings calls in the company's history. NVIDIA came into this quarter facing some serious concerns. Jensen Huang's departure, circular financing, the sustainability of AI spending, declining margins, export restrictions, and whether the company could continue executing without its founder. And I think management did a pretty good job addressing most of them.
First, the numbers were absolutely incredible. NVIDIA reported $116 billion in quarterly revenue, more than doubling year over year and growing 20% sequentially. Data center revenue reached $108 billion, up 21% quarter over quarter, while Vera Rubin generated nearly $20 billion in its first quarter of production shipments, making it the fastest product ramp in NVIDIA's history. Management also guided for $130 billion in Q4 revenue and raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook from 70% to 75%. Think about that for a second. We're talking about a company already generating more than $100 billion in quarterly revenue that still expects 75% annual growth in fiscal 2028. One of the biggest concerns was obviously Jensen Huang's departure. Interestingly, Jensen was only mentioned twice by name during the entire call. It almost felt like management wanted to distance the conversation from Jensen and shift investors' attention back to the business. The board explicitly stated that Jensen would not return as CEO and refused to discuss the ongoing investigation. Instead, Colette emphasized that NVIDIA's employees, leadership team, customers, and suppliers remain fully committed. She even mentioned that TSMC's leadership had been in NVIDIA's offices this week. The company also confirmed that Vera Rubin Ultra remains on track for next year, with Feynman expected in 2028. Now, despite the board saying Jensen isn't coming back, I personally still think there's a small chance we could eventually see him return in some capacity. I wouldn't bet on it, but I wouldn't completely rule it out either.
Another major concern was circular financing, particularly NVIDIA's financial relationships with neoclouds and other AI infrastructure companies. Investors have been worried that NVIDIA is essentially financing customers who then purchase its GPUs. Management clarified that many of its guarantees only take effect once customers have secured financing and their infrastructure is ready for deployment. If those conditions aren't met, certain commitments can be reduced or eliminated. Colette also confirmed this wasn't a new policy, just additional disclosure explaining how the arrangements work. That doesn't eliminate the risk, especially with NVIDIA carrying $118 billion in guarantees and $32 billion in neocloud related commitments, but it does provide more transparency. And speaking of neoclouds, I thought this was one of the most bullish parts of the entire call for companies like $NBIS and $CRWV. NVIDIA's AI Cloud, Industrial, and Enterprise segment generated $47 billion in revenue, growing 18% sequentially and nearly tripling year over year. Management emphasized that neoclouds are becoming increasingly important to the AI ecosystem, helping enterprises, governments, and AI labs access computing capacity.
NVIDIA revealed that Hopper GPUs are being recontracted at up to twice their original rental prices, while B300 rental rates have increased more than 60% since introduction. Management also confirmed that its compute remains fully utilized across every hyperscaler and neocloud it serves. That's a pretty big deal because one of the biggest bearish arguments against neoclouds has been that their expensive GPUs would rapidly lose value as newer hardware became available. Instead, we're seeing older GPUs retain significant economic value while newer hardware commands higher rental rates. $NBIS jumped more than 12% following those comments, and I think it's pretty clear why. If these pricing and utilization trends continue, the economics for well positioned neocloud operators could be considerably better than many investors expected. Another concern was whether the AI infrastructure boom was approaching its peak. NVIDIA pushed back with some pretty incredible numbers. Cloud industry backlog increased from $2 trillion to $2.5 trillion in just three months, while hyperscaler cloud revenue growth accelerated for the sixth consecutive quarter. Meanwhile, token volumes on OpenRouter increased 35 times year over year, with AI agents now accounting for approximately 80% of tokens. Token prices have also declined nearly 60% since May, encouraging significantly greater usage. Essentially, AI is becoming cheaper to use, but consumption is growing so quickly that demand for computing infrastructure continues to accelerate.
Margins were another major topic. NVIDIA expects Q4 gross margins to decline to 71%–72%, but management explicitly described that quarter as the bottom, with margins expected to recover to 72%–73% in fiscal 2028. Colette explained that NVIDIA had honored existing purchase orders despite rising supply costs and expects updated pricing to help stabilize margins. That's reassuring considering the concerns around memory costs, advanced packaging, and competition from custom AI chips. Management also addressed supply constraints, confirming that NVIDIA has secured additional memory and advanced packaging capacity. Vera Rubin is being deployed roughly twice as fast as Grace Blackwell, with hyperscalers bringing the platform into production in approximately one month. NVIDIA is also prioritizing customers that have secured financing, sufficient power, and data centers ready to deploy its hardware. That's particularly important because demand means very little if customers can't actually install and operate the infrastructure.
There were also questions about a potential slowdown in 2028 due to political uncertainty, electricity constraints, and opposition to data center construction. Management acknowledged those risks but emphasized that customers are still requesting more supply than NVIDIA can currently deliver. The company also established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to strengthen engagement with the US government. Importantly, its guidance already excludes future licensed Hopper shipments to China, although the latest export restrictions are still being evaluated. Another encouraging development was capital allocation. NVIDIA returned $28 billion to shareholders during the quarter, including $22 billion in buybacks and $6 billion in dividends. It also increased its repurchase authorization by $150 billion, leaving $227 billion available at quarter-end. Management intends to execute that authorization by the end of fiscal 2028 while continuing to invest in supply chain expansion and selected infrastructure partnerships.
Overall, I think NVIDIA delivered exactly the kind of earnings call investors needed following the uncertainty of the past week. Management addressed nearly every major concern, raised its long-term growth outlook, and showed that demand for AI infrastructure remains exceptionally strong. Of course, Jensen's departure is still a major uncertainty, circular financing risks haven't completely disappeared, and customers will eventually need to demonstrate sufficient returns on their enormous AI investments. But when you have a company generating $116 billion in quarterly revenue, guiding for $130 billion next quarter, and still expecting 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028, it's pretty difficult to argue that the underlying business is falling apart. Whether that's enough to reverse the recent stock decline remains to be seen, but I think NVIDIA gave the bulls plenty of ammunition tonight.

On market crashes like today, I'm reminded of a piece of advice I got from a CIO mentor that traded during the dotcom and 08 crashes and lived to tell the tale.
He said: "Treat investing the same way you treat life."
That's all. It has stuck with me for many years because after filling in the blanks, you're forced to become "better" in both portfolio management and life management. It's uncanny how correlated they are.
Strip either one down and you're left with the same raw materials: time and uncertainty.
Every investment gives up something certain today for something uncertain tomorrow. So does nearly everything that matters in life. Love, learning, raising a child, starting a new job. Anything.
Both reward patience, but only after testing it.
You can't generate performance without risking losses, the same way you can't love without risking grief.
But fundamentally, the first rule of portfolio and life management is survival.
You can come back from most losses, but not from the one that takes you out of the game.
It's always darkest before the dawn.

Interestingly, recent UBS research shows that large IPOs create a pre-IPO liquidity draught which then reverses on IPO launches.
More specifically, in the 3 weeks before IPO, $SPY averages -5.8% when then flips to +9.5% in the 3 months after IPO (on avg.)
We could also see further tailwinds on the run up to 2027 via positive Xmas seasonality and technical alignment (SPY at 200 DMA).
So in my ideal scenario, we see some consolidation around these levels (i.e. no aggressive V-shaped recovery like after July), which in turn would provide hedgies/retail additional confidence that the worst is behind us.
This would also show that the HF community have better risk mgmt frameworks in place because, after all, they failed to prevent concentrated positions in Semis from building back up excessively in Aug-Sep after the July loss. Idiots!!!!
All to say...A LOT of pricing-in has been done, with Jensen's exit being the biggest external shock we'll see for quite some time.
The lingering questions I have are mainly around rates behaving themselves, any more weird cyber attacks, and immedite HF incentives to add risk in the near-term.
HFs have been bleeding for quite some time (as seen with the 13Fs this week), so simply psychology would suggest that they just chill in 2026 before going again in 2027 to save returns accrued YTD.
Retail dip-buying activity has been strong, so we need HFs to follow suit to see any sustained rallies. Flows data in the coming days/week should provide more colour on whether L/S ratio has normalized.
For now, it feels like there are sufficient tailwinds for a short-term / tactical bounce...barring any external shocks.

Markets have now given me PTSD on every green rally.
That being said, $SOI accelerating from $25m quarterly photonics-SOI revenue… with no forward visibility earlier this year.
Into securing $1.2B in agreements this quarter, backed by cash, is extremely transformative and make me happy to see.
In terms transcript details:
- “AI data center have built large compute power, but some of it remains idle as copper links limit data availability for processing.
Optics removes that bottleneck”
Reiterating what I said about aggregate capex not applying 1:1 with optical sector, given optical shifts improves GPU utilization

Co-Packaged Optics for scale out is starting to ramp. TPO for scale up will be the next stage”

In fiscal year 2027, our revenue comes mostly from pluggable transceiver, and we see initial volume from NPO.”
- “Growth returned sooner than we had anticipated and with more vigor. Revenue grew 39%, with Photonics-SOI leading the way.
Margin expansion has come forward too”
- “So, for the capacity reservation agreement we signed, they cover calendar year 2027, calendar year 2028, and beyond”
In terms of where they see acceleration:
- “Now we see and we believe the new requests that we are getting lately are more for the Co-Packaged Optics and NPO. And especially for the scale-up going forward.”
I think that this quarter earnings marks the inflection of optical acceleration for Soitec + silicon photonics.
And what it means for a chokepoint to transform into company economics.

items.title:
Now that we're close to 2027 it's a good idea to stress test downside scenarios where you have:
1. Capex cuts past 2028
2. Stranded Compute / DC Slowdowns
3. Finance deterioration (base case)
4. 2x+ rate hikes
Working in parallel and see what happens with valuations of AI longs.
If you see acceleration despite all 4, I'd argue that's an opportunity.
> Next-gen of photonics is one of the rare segments with an extreme rise in optical content and ASPs that can offset aggregate capex cuts.
Everyone’s moving into that space, including Elon Musk doing M&A, Marvell, Samsung and others with M&A… and we haven’t seen economic impact on emerging architectures even hit players from Celestial to Ayar + their suppliers yet.
If we look at a scenario where there's excess GPUs but power constraints:
We might see slowdown in aggregate accelerator/GPU/ASIC procurement, but your optical engines + light sources + switches players see acceleration.
Especially as incentive to replace power inefficient networking... since different (cheap BOM) optical architectures improves GPU utilization or even HBM requirements.
So value migrates to players more high-beta to architectural shifts.
If Celestial projections are $500m -> $1B, and we expect -30% aggregate capex cuts, I'd argue we'd still see upward revisions from Celestial over the next 2 years.
But financing with #3 matters a lot as seen with $AAOI dropping off of a $550M, vs. $COHR getting prepayments for capacity expansion from their customers.
Companies that rely on external foundries might be less sensitive to #3 since they're not as capex intensive.
On the other hand, companies in sectors have a lot of floating interest like certain Neoclouds, and require further financing might be the most impacted.
> Legacy and specialty memory is a different cycle that markets conflate with AI capex.
If consumer demand weakens but at the same time, players like Windbond exits DDR2, pricing durability is longer than markets expect.
> Wafer/substrate procurement such as ABF, SOI, InP are low cost but large downstream destruction if not secured, so we’ll likely see acceleration here as seen with $NVDA earnings call.
> qualification cycle players within bottlenecks remain very compelling, since first revenue in a large TAM, relative to MC is material to that company.
If a company is valued at $400m then they get a $200m of orders, it's more asymmetrical to a certain company than a rounding error to a $50B incumbent revenue.
_
There’s period of times where prices are dislocated from fundamentals from leveraged players getting wiped. I’d argue that time is now.
I disagree with a lot of the stupid "it's over takes" but I agree it's a good idea to haircut future capex expectations and forward valuations due to financing tightening + macro.
It's also good idea to see the nuances and stress test downside cases.
But TLDR: I'd argue next phase of AI infrastructure is going to be increasingly disconnected from aggregate AI capex growth.
I just personally wrote 4 things I'm using to stress test jointly some of the names I'm looking at, so I'm more comfortable waiting things out... despite seeing hedge funds getting liquidated left and right and overwhelming short positioning.
I personally see acceleration in more narrow parts of the supply chain, while markets treat the entire AI trade as one.
We'll see how things play out on longer horizons.
items.title_ja:
2027 年が近づいている今、次のような下振れシナリオをストレス テストすることをお勧めします。
1. 2028 年を超えて設備投資を削減
2. コンピューティングの孤立 / DC の速度低下
3. 財務悪化（ベースケース）
4. 2倍以上の利上げ
並行して作業し、AI ロングの評価に何が起こるかを確認します。
4 つすべてにもかかわらず加速が見られる場合、それはチャンスだと私は主張します。
> 次世代フォトニクスは、光学コンテンツと ASP が極端に増加しており、総設備投資削減を相殺できる数少ないセグメントの 1 つです。
M&Aを行っているイーロン・マスク、M&Aを行っているマーベル、サムスンなどを含め、誰もがその分野に移行しつつあります...そして、新興アーキテクチャーへの経済的影響は、CelestialからAyarまでのプレーヤーとそのサプライヤーにさえ及んでいるのはまだ見ていません。
GPU が余っているが電力制約があるシナリオを考えてみると、次のようになります。
アクセラレータ/GPU/ASIC の調達全体では減速が見られるかもしれませんが、光学エンジン + 光源 + スイッチ プレーヤーは加速していると考えられます。
特に、さまざまな (安価な BOM) 光学アーキテクチャにより GPU 使用率が向上し、さらには HBM 要件も改善されるため、電力効率の悪いネットワーキングを置き換えるインセンティブとして役立ちます。
したがって、アーキテクチャの変更により、より高ベータのプレイヤーに価値が移行します。
Celestial の予測が 5 億ドル -> 10 億ドルで、設備投資総額が -30% 削減されると予想される場合、今後 2 年間で Celestial による上方修正が見られると私は主張します。
しかし、$AAOI が 5 億 5,000 万ドルを割り込んだのに対し、$COHR が顧客から容量拡張の前払いを受けていることからわかるように、#3 への資金調達は非常に重要です。

items.title:
SOME PERSONAL THOUGHTS AHEAD OF WEEKEND
I wanted to share a few thoughts heading into the weekend because at least for me this has been one of most mentally exhausting stretches I've experienced investing in growth stocks.
And honestly one of the things I've found most difficult has very little to do with market itself since it's how much mental real estate I apparently occupy in the minds of certain "gurus" on this platform whom I've never met, followed or even spoken to.
I started sharing my thoughts on X back in 2023 simply because I genuinely love investing and wanted somewhere to talk about market, share my research and connect with people who enjoyed it as much as I did and I never imagined that would turn into an account reaching 100 million impressions every month or that I'd eventually find myself appearing on national television every week.
I'm incredibly grateful because this platform accelerated my career at a relatively young age and opened doors that otherwise might have taken me many more years to reach but I'd be lying if I said spotlight wasn't intense since the larger my audience becomes and more visible I am the more I've realized that success also seems to attract resentment from people I've never interacted with or affected in any way possible.
Daniel has a phrase for this that I think captures it perfectly because "hating up" is absolutely real especially online where people seem more comfortable attacking someone who has become visible than examining why that person's success bothers them in the first place.
Like I've had people accuse me of taking an investment idea from them despite fact that I don't follow them and have never even seen their work while others take a disagreement over a particular thesis and turn it into a personal judgment about whether I know anything about investing.
What I find especially strange is that some of these individuals are in their 40s and 50s have been doing this for decades and still seem determined to tear down a 33 year old who is simply willing to publish his research, explain what he believes and put his own money behind those convictions (I've never asked anyone to agree with me or suggested that my way of investing is the only way to succeed).
And I think that last part is important because I do all of this under my real name and face, publicly disclose what I own through my subs service, share my position sizes and actual dollars I've invested and expose myself to scrutiny over every good decision and every mistake along the way.
There's absolutely nothing wrong with choosing to remain anonymous and I respect anyone who prefers to operate that way but theres just a different level of personal accountability when people know exactly who you are and watch you explain your thesis on camera and follow your positions in real time and wait for first opportunity to use a bad outcome against you... just remember being wrong privately costs you money but being wrong publicly can also cost you reputation, confidence and peace of mind which is something I don't think people fully appreciate until they've experienced it themselves.
None of this is to suggest that criticism should be off limits because disagreement is a huge part of investing but what I truly struggle to understand is why disagreement so often has to become personal... especially during periods like this when so many people are already dealing with painful drawdowns and questioning decisions they made with the best information available to them.
Markets eventually humble every single one of us regardless of how experienced we are or how much success we've had and anyone who stays in this long enough will eventually experience a thesis that breaks or a position they sized too aggressively or a drawdown that exposes a weakness in their process or a decision they wish they could take back so that's why I think showing people grace matters so much because you never know when you'll find yourself on the other side of that experience hoping others will extend you the same understanding.
And also just remember it cost absolutely nothing to root for people, respect the work they're putting in and recognize that someone can be wrong about an investment without deserving to be ridiculed for it and I genuinely wish more people on this platform understood that being publicly wrong doesn't erase courage it takes to stand behind your own convictions in the first place.
And to the people who've made rooting against me a hobby I genuinely hope you find the same energy for your own work that you've found for mine because if you're spending more time waiting for someone else to fail than building something of your own then maybe my portfolio isn't what needs your attention.
I'll be here next week, same name, same face, same conviction.

週末に向けての個人的な考え
少なくとも私にとって、これは成長株への投資で経験した中で最も精神的に疲れる作業の1つだったので、週末に向けていくつかの考えを共有したいと思いました。
そして正直に言うと、私が最も難しいと感じたことの1つは、市場自体とはほとんど関係がありません。それは、私が会ったことも、フォローしたことも、話したことさえない、このプラットフォーム上の特定の「達人」の心の中で私がどれだけの精神的領域を占めていると思われるかということだからです。
私が X についての考えを 2023 年に共有し始めたのは、単純に投資が心から好きで、市場について話したり、自分の研究を共有したり、同じように市場を楽しんでいる人々とつながる場所が欲しかったからです。それが毎月 1 億インプレッションに達するアカウントに成長したり、最終的には全国放送のテレビに毎週出演するようになるとは想像もしていませんでした。
このプラットフォームのおかげで、比較的若い年齢で私のキャリアが加速し、到達するまでにさらに何年もかかっていた可能性がある扉が開かれたので、非常に感謝しています。しかし、視聴者が増えて知名度が上がるほど、成功は、私がこれまで交流したことのない、あるいは何らかの影響を与えたことのない人たちからの怒りを引き寄せるようにも見えることに気づいたので、スポットライトが強くなかったと言ったら嘘になります。
ダニエルはこれについてのフレーズを持っていますが、これはそれを完璧に捉えていると思います。なぜなら、「憎しみ」は絶対に現実のもので、特にオンラインでは、人々は誰かを調べるよりも、目立つようになった人を攻撃する方が安心しているようです。

SATYA NADELLA: "IF YOU DON'T ACCEPT THE AGENT, SOMEBODY ELSE WILL"
Microsoft $MSFT CEO Satya Nadella said AI agents will reshuffle the economics of the web, at the New York Times DealBook Summit today.
Asked about Amazon blocking outside AI shopping agents from its store, he argued a rival could let agents in and win. "If you don't accept the agent, somebody else will," he said. "If you're in love with a particular business model, you have to kind of scramble."
A day earlier, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said opening Amazon to outside agents "just has to be a good customer experience, which it hasn't been to date."
items.title_ja:
サティア・ナデラ: 「あなたがエージェントを受け入れないなら、他の誰かが受け入れるでしょう。」
Microsoft $MSFT CEO Satya Nadella 氏は、今日の New York Times DealBook Summit で、AI エージェントがウェブの経済性を再編するだろうと述べた。
アマゾンが外部のAIショッピングエージェントを自社の店舗からブロックしていることについて質問された同氏は、ライバルがエージェントを参入させて勝つ可能性があると主張した。 「あなたがその代理人を受け入れなければ、他の誰かが受け入れるでしょう」と彼は言った。 「特定のビジネスモデルに夢中になっている場合は、かなり慌てる必要があります。」
前日、アマゾンの最高経営責任者（CEO）アンディ・ジャシーは、アマゾンを外部代理店に開放することは「優れた顧客体験でなければならないが、これまではそうではなかった」と語った。

WALL STREET'S $500B PLEDGE TO FINANCE NVIDIA $NVDA BUYERS HAS DEPLOYED $0
Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR signed on in August to mobilize $500B so Nvidia's customers could keep buying its chips. Per the WSJ, none of it has gone out, and the first deal isn't expected before next year.
The paper behind it is a few pages long. None of the signers is obliged to raise a dollar, and people involved told the WSJ the $500B figure isn't meaningful.
The fight is over the guarantee. Nvidia limited its backstop to a quarter of each project, while Broadcom covered about 85% of its $35B Anthropic financing.
Apollo CEO Marc Rowan said neoclouds could lose their funding if Nvidia drops the guarantor role.
items.title_ja:
ウォール街が NVIDIA $NVDA に資金を提供するという 5,000 億ドルの約束をした購入者は $0 を導入しました

その後ろにある紙は数ページあります。署名者の誰も1ドルを調達する義務はなく、関係者らはWSJに対し、5000億ドルという数字には意味がないと語った。
ギャラをめぐる戦いは終わった。 Nvidia はバックストップを各プロジェクトの 4 分の 1 に限定したが、Broadcom は 350 億ドルの Anthropic 資金調達の約 85% をカバーした。
Apolloの最高経営責任者（CEO）マーク・ローワン氏は、NVIDIAが保証人の役割をやめればネオクラウドは資金を失う可能性があると述べた。

Anthropic would need about $602 billion in annual revenue to earn a 20% return on its roughly $1 trillion in compute commitments, per FT
The math: a 20% return on $1 trillion is $200 billion in after-tax profit. At a 17% tax rate, that’s about $241 billion before tax, and at a 40% operating margin, it takes about $602 billion in revenue.
That’s more than Alphabet’s $471 billion or Apple’s $478 billion in annual revenue. It’s about two-thirds of the $908 billion earned by all 76 software and IT services companies in the S&P 1500 combined.
For comparison, Anthropic’s annualized revenue run rate hit $81 billion at the end of October. Goldman, the lead underwriter, projects revenue of more than $600 billion by 2030.

計算すると、1 兆ドルに対する 20% の利益は、税引き後利益で 2,000 億ドルとなります。税率 17% の場合、税引前で約 2,410 億ドル、営業利益率 40% の場合、売上高は約 6,020 億ドルとなります。
これはアルファベットの年間売上高4,710億ドルやアップルの年間売上高4,780億ドルを上回ります。これは、S&P 1500 に含まれるソフトウェアおよび IT サービス企業 76 社すべてが稼いだ 9,080 億ドルの約 3 分の 2 に相当します。
